result:
I changed the backend so inline and shared metrics on an experiment no longer end up with the same identifier. I did not run any tests or add a new one, so none of this is verified.

- **Promotion (`experiment_saved_metric_service.py`):** `create_saved_metric` now drops any incoming `uuid` from the query and gives the new shared metric a fresh one. A promoted metric no longer inherits the identifier of the inline metric it was copied from. Any existing test that creates a saved metric with a client-supplied `uuid` and expects it kept will now fail.
- **Attach-only update (`experiment_service.py`):** when an update carries `saved_metrics_ids` but not `metrics` or `metrics_secondary`, the stored inline lists are now checked against the attached shared metrics' identifiers. If an inline metric clashes, that list goes through the existing dedup step, so the inline metric gets a new identifier and the shared metric keeps its own. The existing ordering sync then handles the swap. I haven't traced that sync end to end, so an edge case there could still remove the shared metric's entry from the ordering arrays.
- **Agent guidance (`metric-configuration.md.j2`):** it no longer tells agents to create a shared metric with the same query and attach it. It now says to remove the inline copy in the same update, since keeping both would show the same metric twice.
